messages:
ashley: Heads-up — MapleHealth reports objects with default 90d retention still visible after TTL expiry. Legal wants preservation but customer sees records in search. Case 7421, escalating.

liz: Can you paste a minimal repro and a couple object IDs? also which API calls return what (GET vs delete status)?

ashley: Sample obj ids: obj-6f7a2c, obj-9b2d11. Created 2025-11-01, retention=90d. Expected deletion ~2026-02-01. GET /v1/objects/obj-6f7a2c -> 200 + body. Storage tombstone shows present. Audit log snippet below:

```
DELETE scheduled: 2026-02-01T03:12:07Z org=maplehealth obj=obj-6f7a2c status=queued
delete.worker: processing obj-6f7a2c started
delete.worker: obj-6f7a2c failed error=KMS_DECRYPT_FAILURE key=key-77
```

pradeep: Sounds like index vs physical deletion discrepancy or KMS failures during tombstone sealing. Any KMS/HSM errors in audit? also was there any custom retention policy for this org overriding default?

ashley: Customer did not set custom retention. They are on default 90d. I pulled KMS audit and see repeated decrypt failures around 2026-02-01: `kms.hsm auth=403 key=key-77 op=decrypt host=hsm-3`.

cody: We had a scheduled HSM key rotation on 2026-02-01 for key-77 (rolling keys across HSMs). If workers attempted to tombstone while rotation was mid-flight, decrypt/encrypt calls could fail and the deletion job would mark failed but search index might still return the object.

legal-team: Customer also opened a preservation request on 2026-02-15. We need a clean audit export covering created/deleted/hold actions and a guaranteed freeze of any further deletes until legal confirms.

ashley: Customer is panicking — says records must be preserved for litigation. They want confirmation that nothing was permanently lost.

cody: Immediate mitigation: pause deletion queue for org maplehealth, and run a backfill that re-checks tombstones and re-enqueues deletions only after successful KMS ops. I can run once approved.

liz: Is this a policy precedence bug? default retention should win when custom is absent. If rotation causes transient KMS 403s, purge should retry not silently mark success/fail wrongly. Tagging for product/infra follow-up.

pradeep: Agree. From storage side, mark as `needs-repro`. Likely root cause: deletion worker marks obj as "processed" when index removal succeeded but storage encryption failed, leaving visible record. We'll need to repro in staging with key rotation.

ashley: Quick repro steps I ran in non-prod:
1) create object with retention=90
2) simulate KMS 403 on decrypt during delete worker
3) run delete worker -> observe index removed but GET still returns object body

curl snippets:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/objects -d '{"id":"obj-test-1","retention":90}'
curl -X GET https://api.redwood/v1/objects/obj-test-1
# simulate KMS 403 (test hook)
# run delete worker
```

pradeep: Good repro. I'll add a test for rotation window and ensure delete worker idempotency and stronger success criteria (both index AND storage sealed).

cody: For now I'll pause deletes and start an export. Commands I'm going to run after legal ok: 
```
redwood-admin retention pause --org maplehealth
redwood-admin retention backfill --org maplehealth --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-03-01 --verify-kms
```

support-bot: Escalation created INC-2026-1543, SLA timer 4h, assigned to pradeep + cody.

legal-team: Please hold any destructive ops until we validate audit export. We need items: object id, creation time, TTL policy, deletion attempts, KMS error traces.

ashley: Copy — starting collection and will attach to INC-2026-1543. Also looping in product to evaluate if default-vs-custom precedence logic needs a maintenance notice.

pradeep: setting label `needs-repro` and will schedule staging run for tomorrow.

cody: paused deletion queue for maplehealth and kicking off export to /exports/INC-2026-1543/maplehealth-audit-20260302.tar.gz. Will report back when export completes.

ashley: thanks — please @me when export ready, legal will review and then we can unblock. :white_check_mark:
